blogs.title: The Pulmonary Mask: When Recurrent Pleural Effusions Hide a Pancreatic Secret
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic pitfall of Pancreatopleural Fistula (PPF), emphasizing how it frequently mimics primary thoracic pathology like tuberculosis or malignancy. We will analyze why clinicians often exhaust pulmonary workups before considering an abdominal source, highlighting the critical importance of re-taking the trauma history and recognizing that 'respiratory distress' does not always equal 'lung disease.'

blogs.title: Beyond TB and Malignancy: Interpreting Hemorrhagic, Amylase-Rich Pleural Fluid
blogs.description: Focusing on laboratory diagnostics, this article dissects the differential diagnosis for hemorrhagic pleural effusions with elevated adenosine deaminase (ADA) and amylase. We will discuss the specific utility of pleural fluid amylase levels (>1000 IU/L) and isoform typing (pancreatic vs. salivary) to distinguish PPF from esophageal perforation, malignancy, and tuberculous pleurisy, preventing unnecessary antitubercular therapy or oncologic staging.

blogs.title: From Handlebars to Hydrothorax: The Unique Etiology of Pediatric Pancreatic Trauma
blogs.description: Unlike adults where alcohol-induced chronic pancreatitis dominates, pediatric PPF is frequently traumatic or genetic. This post reviews the mechanism of blunt abdominal trauma (e.g., bicycle handlebars) causing posterior pancreatic duct disruption and retroperitoneal tracking through the diaphragmatic hiatus. We will also touch upon when to suspect underlying genetic mutations (PRSS1, SPINK1) in children presenting with spontaneous or minor-trauma-induced pancreatitis.

blogs.title: Imaging the Invisible Tract: Why MRCP Trumps CT in Suspected Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: A technical deep-dive into radiological strategies for PPF. While CT scans effectively identify pseudocysts and consolidations, they often fail to visualize the actual fistulous tract. This post argues for the early utilization of Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) as the diagnostic modality of choice to map ductal anatomy and confirm the fistula, potentially sparing patients from invasive diagnostic procedures like ERCP unless therapeutic intervention is immediately required.

blogs.title: Conservative First? Navigating the Medical Management Algorithm for Pediatric PPF
blogs.description: With no standardized guidelines for pediatric PPF, this post evaluates the step-wise treatment approach starting with bowel rest, Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN), and somatostatin analogues (Octreotide). We will review the evidence behind using Octreotide to suppress exocrine secretion, discuss the realistic success rates of conservative management versus endoscopic stenting or surgery, and outline clear criteria for escalating care when drainage fails to resolve.
